rationale: The Latin anchors *germen* (shoot, bud, sprout) and *festuca* (stalk, stem, blade) point firmly to a small, living plant growth — a shoot or young twig — rather than an ornamental representation. The quasi-poetic gloss "quasi stillæ super graminum germina" (like drops upon the shoots/germs of grasses) further confirms a literal, botanical sense matching branchlet.n.01 (a small terminal branch or shoot), as opposed to the decorative/ornamental sense of sprig.n.02.
